headline: Attackers piled onto freshly disclosed SharePoint, SonicWall, and Oracle flaws while AI tools powered both new malware and a White House vulnerability clearinghouse.

emerging_trends.text: Criminals increasingly build their malware with large language models, as Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 dissected TuxBot v3, an IoT botnet framework whose code still carried the AI's safety disclaimer that its developer forgot to strip out.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Coding Tools Weaponized and LLM-Built Malware

emerging_trends.text: Poisoned open-source packages keep landing on npm, where five compromised AsyncAPI releases delivered a multi-stage botnet loader and credential stealer just days after the last cleanup.
Enterprise edge appliances remain the softest target, with SonicWall confirming two SMA 1000 zero-days under active attack as CISA logged fresh exploitation of Oracle and SharePoint bugs.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Active Exploitation of SharePoint, SonicWall, and Oracle Flaws

topics.title: Active Exploitation of SharePoint, SonicWall, and Oracle Flaws
topics.latest_developments: CISA on July 15, 2026 added Oracle E-Business Suite privilege-management flaw CVE-2026-46817 and KNX protocol flaw CVE-2023-4346 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, SonicWall confirmed attackers are exploiting two SMA 1000 zero-days—including SSRF bug CVE-2026-15409 rated 10.0 that yields arbitrary command execution—and Zoom warned of a critical unauthenticated account-takeover flaw in its Windows desktop client and SDK.
topics.summary: CISA urged administrators to patch three actively exploited on-premises SharePoint Server flaws that attackers chain for remote code execution on internet-exposed instances. Organizations running SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances, Oracle E-Business Suite, or the Zoom Windows client should apply vendor fixes immediately.

sources.title: Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days Exploited, One Could Enable Admin Commands
CISA warns admins to patch actively exploited SharePoint flaws
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
Zoom warns of critical account takeover vulnerability

topics.title: Record Patch Tuesday Fallout
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft blocked this month's Windows 11 security updates on some Dell devices after the patches triggered shutdowns and performance drops, Ars Technica detailed the LegacyHive proof-of-concept as a powerful privilege-escalation primitive against the Windows User Profile Service, Siemens, Schneider Electric, and Rockwell Automation fixed dozens of ICS flaws on the same Patch Tuesday, and Mozilla and Google shipped Firefox 152 and Chrome 150 to close critical flaws whose exploit code is already public.
topics.summary: Microsoft's record 622-CVE July Patch Tuesday continues to reverberate as researcher Chaotic Eclipse's LegacyHive PoC surfaces a day later. Administrators should stage the Windows updates, patch browsers and ICS gear, and heed the Dell shutdown block.

sources.title: Windows 0-day drops the same day Microsoft releases record number of patches
Microsoft: Some Dell PCs shut down after recent Windows updates
ICS Patch Tuesday: Vulnerabilities Fixed by Siemens, Schneider, Rockwell
Firefox, Chrome, Adobe, and VMware Updates Fix Multiple Critical Security Flaws

topics.title: AI Coding Tools Weaponized and LLM-Built Malware
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 dissected TuxBot v3 Evolution, an IoT botnet framework whose LLM-written code still carried the model's safety disclaimer, and Dark Reading detailed Anthropic's now-patched PromptFiction flaw that automatically fed malicious prompts to Claude agents, both surfacing alongside the still-unpatched Cursor code-execution bug and the Gemini CLI abuse by Russian-speaking actor bandcampro.
topics.summary: Threat actors now build malware with large language models and bend AI developer tools into attack vectors, including a git.exe that Cursor silently runs from a cloned repository root on Windows. Developers should treat cloned repositories as untrusted and keep AI coding assistants patched and sandboxed.

sources.title: TuxBot v3: Inside an IoT Botnet Framework With LLM-Assisted Development
Claude Flaw Automatically Sends Malicious Prompts to AI Agents
Cursor Flaw Lets Malicious Cloned Repositories Trigger Windows Code Execution
Google Gemini CLI abused as a hacking agent, malware botnet operator

topics.title: npm and GitHub Supply-Chain Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Five malicious @asyncapi npm package versions delivered a multi-stage botnet loader and an info-stealing remote access trojan, Unit 42 published an updated npm threat landscape tracing wormable malware and CI/CD persistence after Shai Hulud, and Arctic Wolf found a financially motivated actor impersonating 292 brands across GitHub repositories to push smash-and-grab infostealers.
topics.summary: Open-source registries and code-hosting platforms remain prime malware-delivery channels, with the newly documented LabubaRAT posing as NVIDIA software to plant a reusable Windows foothold. Developers should pin dependency versions and verify download sources.

sources.title: AsyncAPI npm packages infected with credential-stealing malware

topics.title: White House Gold Eagle AI Vulnerability Clearinghouse
topics.latest_developments: The White House launched Gold Eagle on July 15, 2026, an AI-driven clearinghouse that lets industry, critical-infrastructure operators, and government agencies detect, prioritize, and patch vulnerabilities faster, a program stemming from the AI-focused executive order President Trump signed June 2, 2026.
topics.summary: Gold Eagle applies artificial intelligence to coordinate vulnerability disclosure and remediation across the public and private sectors. It arrives with fresh CISA and NSA guidance urging software makers to run coordinated vulnerability disclosure programs with outside researchers.

sources.title: White House Launches AI-Driven 'Gold Eagle' Vulnerability Coordination Initiative
Trump administration unveils AI-supported clearinghouse for cyber vulnerabilities
Establishing a Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Program to Work With Security Researchers

topics.title: Dutch Police Dismantle €100 Million Investment Fraud Ring
topics.latest_developments: Dutch police arrested the alleged mastermind and several members of an international crypto-investment fraud ring that ran about two dozen call centers and employed more than 700 people posing as professional financial advisers, stealing over €100 million from tens of thousands of victims since at least 2021.
topics.summary: The scheme operated like a legitimate cross-border business, defrauding tens of thousands of victims. It caps a week of European fraud takedowns, including a €140 million network the Spanish National Police dismantled days earlier.

sources.title: Dutch police bust investment fraud ring stealing over €100 million
Dutch police dismantle global crypto investment scam, arrest alleged mastermind

business_politics.title: Oil Supply Crunch as Hormuz Shuts Again
business_politics.latest_developments: U.S. forces struck a tanker bound for Iran's Kharg Island oil terminal under the renewed blockade, and traders warn the commercial stockpiles that cushioned the war's early shocks now run low as the Strait of Hormuz closes again.
business_politics.summary: The United States reimposed a naval blockade of Iran and stepped up airstrikes after Iranian forces fired on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, the passage for roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil; crude climbed as thinning stockpiles raised the threat of a global supply crunch.
